title: What does the XRPL RequireDest account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of RequireDest and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, RequireDest requires incoming payments to carry a destination tag, represented in AccountRoot by RequireDestTag. [1]

A tag identifies a customer or purpose in the receiver's own system. Requiring its presence does not establish that the supplied number maps to the intended beneficiary. The receiving business still needs a correct mapping. Keep the tag with the verified destination address throughout payment preparation, rather than substituting a number inferred from a display name. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for RequireDest and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why RequireDest is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
